decisions.decision: Measured baseline, to be treated as fact and not re-derived by the implementer. internal/update is two files (update.go 5105 bytes, update_test.go 2106 bytes) with exactly two top-level tests, both passing: TestInstallSwitchAndRollbackKeepBothVersions and TestVerifyRejectsTamperAndIncompatibleSchema (measured by devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/update ./cmd/bootstrap; cmd/bootstrap reports '[no test files]'). The package exports ManifestSchema='agentic-loop/module-manifest/v1', Manifest{Schema,Version,OS,Architecture,BinarySHA256,SchemaMin,SchemaMax}, Bundle{Manifest,Binary,Signature}, Verify, Install and Switch. Verify checks an Ed25519 signature over manifest||sha256(binary), decodes the manifest with DisallowUnknownFields plus a single-JSON-value check, requires exact ManifestSchema equality, GOOS/GOARCH equality, BinarySHA256 agreement and currentSchema inside the closed interval [SchemaMin,SchemaMax]. Install writes versions/<version>/{runner 0500, manifest.json 0400} through MkdirTemp+Rename and is idempotent only when the existing bytes match. Switch creates .<channel>.next and renames it over root/<channel>, for channel in {stable,preview}. cmd/bootstrap has verbs install|switch|--version only. internal/update imports only the standard library and its ci/components.json component declares zero dependencies; cmd/bootstrap/** and internal/runner/** belong to the runner component, whose declared dependencies are domain and update. Only cmd/bootstrap/main.go and internal/release/source_guard_test.go reference internal/update anywhere in the tree.
decisions.rationale: Every decision below is an edit to this exact surface. dp-v2-021 d1 established that re-proving measured behaviour spends implementer context; the inverse risk is worse here, because an implementer who assumes internal/update is empty will rewrite Verify and lose the schema-interval semantics that turn out to be the coexist mechanism (d9).

decisions.decision: Signing keys: separate the private release key from the machine trust anchor, and keep both outside the repository (task non_goal 1). Local phase: exactly one Ed25519 private key exists, on the owner's release machine only, at an owner-only 0600 path under the owner's config directory (for example ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}/agentic-loop/signing/release-ed25519.key). It is never on a Runner machine that only consumes bundles, never inside a bundle, a workspace, a data root, an evidence record or a document. The trust anchor is the public half, replicated to each machine out of band as a 0400 file at a fixed absolute path derived from a machine configuration root (for example ${AGENTIC_LOOP_ROOT}/trust/release-keys), holding one accepted key per line as 'key_id base64(pubkey)'. Because machines are never shared and there are two of them, key rotation is inherently two-step per machine, so the anchor is a set, not a single key: add the new key id to both machines, sign with it, then remove the old id. GCP phase: the private half moves to Cloud KMS asymmetric-sign and the signer calls KMS instead of reading a file; the anchor on each machine stays a public key file and the verify path in internal/update does not change at all. The only migration artifacts are (a) the manifest's key_id selects which anchor entry verifies, and (b) an algorithm label per anchor entry so a KMS key whose algorithm is not Ed25519 can be added as a second accepted entry during the overlap.
decisions.rationale: The requirement 'owner 1, machines 2, machines are not shared, only the repository is shared' makes any design that stores the private key where both Runners can read it strictly worse than one that does not, and makes single-key rotation impossible without a window in which one machine rejects valid bundles. Keeping the anchor a file in both phases is what makes the KMS migration a signer-side change rather than a Bootstrapper change, which matters because the Bootstrapper is the one component that cannot self-update (d6).

decisions.decision: Fail-closed verification: the trust anchor must not be an argv-supplied path. Measured defect: cmd/bootstrap install takes --public-key <path> and passes whatever it reads to update.Install, so the process asks its caller for its own trust anchor and a caller who can choose the key can install any binary; the signature check is then decorative. V2-034 resolves the anchor from the fixed machine path of d2 and refuses to run when the anchor file is absent, not a regular file, not owned by the invoking user, not mode 0400/0600, empty, or contains no parsable entry. Any of those refusals exits non-zero before versions/ is touched and before any child process is started; no default key, no 'insecure' flag, no environment override that is not itself an absolute path whose ownership and mode are checked. The refusal shape is the one V2-046 already established in internal/runner/confinement.go: NamespaceConfinement.Probe returns ErrNamespaceUnsupported and no child is launched, rather than degrading to an unconfined run.
decisions.rationale: A fail-closed claim is only worth what its negative tests prove, and the negative case that matters here is not a tampered binary (already covered by TestVerifyRejectsTamperAndIncompatibleSchema) but a substituted key, which no current test or code path prevents. Reusing V2-046's Probe shape keeps one refusal idiom in the Runner-side code instead of two.

decisions.decision: Digest and signature are both required and neither substitutes for the other, and a third digest must be joined to them. Manifest.BinarySHA256 binds this manifest to these binary bytes (tamper detection, and the only thing that lets a launcher re-verify bytes already on disk). The Ed25519 signature over manifest||sha256(binary) binds that pair to the owner's key (provenance: it answers 'who authorised this', which a digest can never answer because an attacker who replaces the binary also replaces the digest). V2-021's release BundleDigest is a third, different thing: sha256 over the framing role\0path\0sha256\n of the seven source roles, which contains no binary at all, so it answers 'which source tree was gated' and cannot answer 'which bytes will execute'. The measured hole is that nothing joins them: a signed bundle today can carry any binary from any tree. V2-034 closes it by adding bundle_digest, candidate_id and contract_release to the module manifest, so the signature covers them and the launcher can state that the binary it is about to exec came from the source tree the promotion gate approved. internal/release must still not import internal/update and internal/update must remain standard-library-only: the join is a value copied into the manifest at build time, not a code edge, preserving dp-v2-021 d12 and its go/ast guard.
decisions.rationale: The brief asks whether both are needed. Measured, they answer disjoint questions and the union is still insufficient, because the release gate's identity at M5-local is a source manifest with no binary in it (dp-v2-021 d3 says so explicitly and defers the binary digest to V2-022 and V2-034). Adding the join as manifest data rather than as an import is the only form that does not create a component edge ci/components.json would then have to record, which is V2-045's territory and prohibited here.

decisions.decision: Module manifest schema evolution: take the one breaking change now, then be additive forever. Measured constraint: Verify requires manifest.Schema to equal ManifestSchema exactly and decodes with DisallowUnknownFields, so adding any field makes every already-installed Bootstrapper reject every new bundle, and the Bootstrapper is precisely the component that cannot be auto-updated (d6). Because no Stable release exists yet and no Bootstrapper is deployed anywhere, V2-034 may bump the schema id once to 'agentic-loop/module-manifest/v2' carrying the d4 fields, and must at the same time replace the single constant with an ordered set AcceptedManifestSchemas so that later evolution is expand-coexist-migrate-contract at the manifest level too: a new id is added to the accepted set in a Bootstrapper release, bundles start declaring it only after both machines accept it, and the old id is removed from the set only after no installed version still declares it. The accepted set is data in internal/update, asserted by a test that a manifest declaring an unaccepted id is refused and that a manifest declaring an accepted older id still verifies.
decisions.rationale: This is the infinite-regress trap in concrete form: the only way to change the bundle format is through the component that only a human can change, so the format must be made evolvable in the one release where breaking it costs nothing. An implementer who simply adds fields to the v1 struct produces a design that can never be changed again without an owner-attended visit to two machines.

decisions.decision: Independent Bootstrapper: 'the process that updates X must not be X' is satisfied structurally, not by convention. The Bootstrapper is a separate binary (cmd/bootstrap) in a separate directory from the Runner, linking only internal/update, and the Runner must not link internal/update at all. Measured, it does not today; V2-034 turns that into a guard rather than luck, with a go/ast import test (the shape of internal/release/source_guard_test.go) asserting that no file under cmd/runner/** or internal/runner/** imports internal/update, and that internal/update's non-test files import only the standard library. V2-034 adds the missing verb: bootstrap run --channel stable|preview resolves root/<channel> to versions/<v>, re-verifies versions/<v>/runner bytes against versions/<v>/manifest.json before every exec (install-time verification says nothing about the bytes on disk now), probes confinement, and starts the Runner as a child in its own process group. An update is therefore: parent installs the new version side by side, flips the symlink, stops the child, starts a new child from the new symlink target. The process being replaced never performs the install and never execs itself.
decisions.rationale: Measured gap: cmd/bootstrap has no run verb and nothing anywhere in the tree reads root/stable, so 'recover from the Stable launcher' has no implementation to recover with. The child-restart formulation is what makes the requirement structural: there is no code path in which the Runner can install or switch, because the symbols are not in its binary.

decisions.decision: The Bootstrapper's own update stays outside self-update, and the regress stops there explicitly. The bundle format has no bootstrapper role and the launcher refuses to install any bundle that declares one, so a compromised or buggy release cannot replace the component that verifies releases. Replacing the launcher, or changing the trust anchor set, is an owner-attended out-of-band procedure per machine: place the new binary or anchor line, verify its digest by hand against the release record, restart the launcher. That is acceptable only because the launcher's attack surface and change rate are deliberately minimal: no network, no Provider, no canonical store, no workspace; its whole input set is (anchor set, bundle bytes, root path, channel). The runbook states this as a standing property and records that a launcher change is a human decision that does not pass through the Loop's own promotion gate.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/technology.md line 225 already fixes this ('Bootstrapper自身は自動更新対象から外し、人間承認の別手順でのみ更新する') and docs/operations/self-update.md repeats it; the design's job is to say where the regress stops and why stopping there is safe, which is the minimal-input-set argument, not to reopen the decision.

decisions.decision: Module version manifest contents: five coordinates in one signed record, plus one machine-local record. Signed per version: (1) binary: version (semver) and binary_sha256; (2) canonical schema: the closed interval [schema_min, schema_max] this binary can operate against, which already exists and is the coexist mechanism, not a validation detail; (3) contract: contract_release and contract_digest, plus the Runner API compatibility range runner_api_min/runner_api_max; (4) bundle: bundle_digest and candidate_id from V2-021's assembly; (5) provenance: key_id and algorithm from d2. Machine-local and not canonical: root/state/installed.json, listing every installed version with its install time, the current stable and preview targets, the previous stable target, the last switch and its reason, and rolled_back_at when a version was switched away from by a rollback. installed.json is the only input the GC predicate (d12) and the rollback window (d13) read besides an injected clock, and it is written after the filesystem operation it describes so a crash leaves it stale-but-safe rather than describing a state that does not exist.
decisions.rationale: release-contract.md section 4 item 8 requires implementation, schema, migration, configuration and documentation to be promotable as one version; a version record that carries only a binary digest cannot express that, and a record that carries the source bundle digest but not the schema interval cannot express coexistence. Keeping installed.json machine-local is forced by the premise that machines are not shared: a canonical record of 'what is installed' would be wrong on both machines for most of every update.

decisions.decision: The mixed-version period is unavoidable and is exactly the coexist stage. Because machines are not shared, two Runners cannot be switched atomically, so there is always an interval in which machine A runs version N+1 and machine B runs version N. The governing invariant is stated over the schema intervals of d8: at every instant, the current canonical schema must lie inside the intersection of the [schema_min, schema_max] intervals of every version that any machine can currently route to (stable, preview and previous stable on both machines). Consequences: a version may be switched onto a machine only if the canonical schema is inside its interval; the canonical schema may advance only into the intersection; and a schema advance that would empty the intersection is refused, not scheduled. V2-034 enforces the half of this that a single machine can see: the launcher refuses to switch onto a version whose interval excludes the canonical schema it reads, and records the interval of every installed version in installed.json. The other half, enforcing the intersection across both machines, requires the Control Plane to know which binary version and interval each Runner is running; measured, it cannot: internal/api carries only a static response 'schema_version':'v1' and optimistic-concurrency Expected*Version fields, there is no version field on any Runner-facing request, and internal/domain has no Runner aggregate at all (only a RunnerID string type). That surface is escalation E1 and must not be invented inside an update-gated task.
decisions.rationale: This is the decision the premise forces: 'machine is not shared, so simultaneous update is impossible' is not a risk to mitigate but a state to make legal and bounded. Expressing it as an interval intersection makes it checkable from data that already exists in the manifest, and separates the part V2-034 can honestly close from the part that needs an API and a domain aggregate that do not exist.

decisions.decision: Firestore schema expand-coexist-migrate-contract, per stage, over the measured codec. Measured: internal/store/firestore stores {record_schema, kind, payload} where payload is a JSON string; RecordSchema is the constant 'v1'; both DecodeRecord (store.go:79) and decodeDocument (store.go:173) refuse with ErrInvalidSchema when d.RecordSchema != RecordSchema; payload decoding is a plain json.Unmarshal, so unknown payload fields are ignored and absent fields default. Therefore: EXPAND writes the new payload field in addition to the old one under the unchanged record_schema; no reader change is needed because unknown-field tolerance already holds; the canonical schema counter goes N to N+1 and the new binary declares [N, N+1]. Fully reversible: the old binary keeps reading the old field. COEXIST is the period in which both binaries run and every reader resolves a value as 'new field if present else old field'; this period is exactly the mixed-version window of d9 and lasts at least until both machines are switched. Fully reversible. MIGRATE is a bounded, resumable, idempotent backfill that rewrites old documents to carry the new field, shaped like a reconcile tick (at most 100 documents per tick, 30 s per tick, restartable from a stored cursor, no wall-clock dependence, no unbounded query: validation.md section 5). Still reversible, because expand never removed the old field. CONTRACT stops writing the old field, deletes it, and where the envelope itself must change, bumps record_schema. Contract is the first irreversible stage and is always a separate Increment from its expand.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 2 lists 'schema expand／coexist／migrate／contract' under emulator-backed store integration tests, and roadmap section 6 requires the old module to be deleted in a later Increment after the rollback window. The four stages are only meaningful if each one names an operation on a real document shape; describing them abstractly is what lets an implementer collapse expand and contract into one release and destroy the rollback path.

decisions.decision: Reversibility boundary and the envelope-coexist gap. Rollback is possible during expand, coexist and migrate, and impossible after contract: a binary whose schema_max is below the post-contract schema can no longer read the store, so its rollback window is closed by the contract step itself rather than by a timer. Contract may therefore run only when, for every version still routable on any machine and for the current stable and previous stable, schema_min is at least the post-contract schema; that is the same predicate as GC eligibility (d12), used a second time. Measured blocker for the envelope half: because both readers compare record_schema with !=, documents written under a new envelope id are invisible to the current reader, so envelope-level coexistence is impossible today and a record_schema bump would be an immediate outage rather than a stage. Widening the readers to an accepted set {v1, v2} is itself the expand step for the envelope and must land before any bump. That widening touches internal/store/firestore/**, which is the store-firestore component (declared dependencies domain and application), not update; pulling it into an update-gated task would add components to the task and to the M8 gate row. It is escalation E2 for Sol to assign, and it blocks V2-035's 'roll back without losing shared state' condition, so it must be assigned before V2-035, not after.
decisions.rationale: The honest statement of where irreversibility begins is the deliverable, and it cannot be written truthfully without naming the one place where the current code makes the coexist stage unreachable. Escalating rather than silently widening the store keeps the component boundary that dp-v2-021 d12 and V2-045 exist to protect.

decisions.decision: Old binary GC binds to release.RetentionEligible's three refusals by value, not by import, and adds two refusals that only exist once binaries are real. The predicate for deleting versions/<v> on a machine is: refuse if v is the current stable route target; refuse if v is the previous stable route target; refuse while its rollback window is open (injected clock against a contract-declared duration, never the clock alone); refuse if any Requirement's StableSnapshot references it; and additionally refuse if v is the target of any channel symlink on this machine, because RetentionEligible knows stable and previous-stable but not preview, which is a live pointer; and refuse if deleting v would leave no retained version whose [schema_min, schema_max] contains the current canonical schema, because that would make the rollback window unsatisfiable while it is still open. Since internal/release must not be imported from internal/update and vice versa (dp-v2-021 d12, enforced by go/ast), the predicate is re-expressed in internal/update over the same inputs and a test asserts case-by-case agreement with release.RetentionEligible's four outcomes on identical inputs, which is a value-level equivalence, not a code edge. Deletion order is crash-safe: re-read every channel symlink immediately before deleting, refuse if the target is reachable from any of them, rename the directory aside and then remove it, and update installed.json afterwards. The bundle carries the Stable and Preview documents of its version (technology.md section 7), so this single predicate is also what satisfies release-contract.md section 5's requirement to retain a rollback target's user documents; there is not a second docs-retention rule.
decisions.rationale: The brief requires that 'cannot be deleted while the rollback window is open' follow from the version manifest rather than from a timer, and that is exactly what the last two refusals add: the first four refusals are route- and reference-shaped, and only the schema-interval refusal ties deletability to the manifest. One predicate covering binaries and their documents is also what makes roadmap M8's fourth completion condition a single check instead of two that can disagree.

decisions.decision: The rollback window is a conjunction, and its closure is recorded rather than inferred. A version stays inside the window while any of the following still holds: it is the previous stable route target (generation criterion: the window opens when a successor becomes Stable and cannot close while nothing newer has been Stable); a contract-stage schema step has not yet moved the canonical schema outside its [schema_min, schema_max] (schema-stage criterion); a contract-declared minimum dwell has not yet elapsed on an injected clock since the successor became Stable (time criterion, so a rapid succession of releases cannot evict the only rollback target); and the successor does not yet hold a passed Preview capability exercise for the whole Release Contract (evidence criterion, so a rollback target is never dropped in favour of an unproven successor). The window closes only when all four have ceased to hold, and closure is written as window_closed_at plus the criterion that closed it, into installed.json and the release record; nothing recomputes closure from the wall clock at read time. What becomes irreversible when it closes: the binary and its bundled documents become GC-eligible, so after deletion returning to that version requires rebuilding and re-signing from source and the cheap route rollback (a symlink flip) is gone; and if closure was caused by a schema contract step, the store no longer serves a shape that version can read, so even a rebuilt binary cannot be routed. That second case is the only one-way transition in M8. Separately, V2-034 must mirror the monotonic-rollback fix dp-v2-021 d8 made in release.Router onto the update side: measured, update.Switch will flip stable to any installed version with no record, no monotonicity and no gate, which is the same ping-pong defect, so Switch must record every switch with its reason, refuse a second consecutive rollback, and require the forward direction to name a gate-passed candidate digest.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 8 forbids expiring evidence on the clock alone, so a purely time-based window would contradict the release contract; a purely generation-based window would close the instant a successor is promoted, which is when rollback is most likely to be needed. Recording closure is what makes the GC predicate reproducible after the fact, and mirroring the monotonicity fix prevents the update layer from re-introducing a defect the release layer already paid to remove.

decisions.decision: Classification of the six decisions by the environment grade that can prove them, cross-checked against roadmap M8's four completion conditions and release-contract.md section 3. Local closure (V2-034, hermetic, no deploy): the fail-closed signature and anchor refusals; the digest/signature/bundle_digest join as manifest data; the accepted-manifest-schema set; the import guards making the Bootstrapper independent; bootstrap run plus per-launch re-verification and child restart; the version manifest fields and the single-machine interval check; the four schema stages and the reversibility boundary over an injected codec port; the GC predicate and its crash-safe deletion; the rollback window predicate and its recorded closure; the monotonic Switch. preview-local (V2-035, real processes, real CLI, Firestore emulator, owner machine): the new Loop deploying its own next version to Preview; breaking a real Preview Control Plane and Runner and recovering through the Stable launcher; rolling back without losing shared canonical state; two roots or machines running different versions simultaneously and both making progress. preview-gcp (D1 / V2-054, and beyond M8): KMS-backed signing, Artifact Registry distribution, and the deploy path itself; none of these appear in M8's completion conditions and neither V2-034 nor V2-035 may claim them. Mapping to roadmap M8's conditions: condition 1 (a new Loop deploys its own new version to Preview) is preview-local live, V2-035; condition 2 (break the Preview Control Plane and Runner, recover from the Stable launcher) is preview-local live, V2-035, and is a Loop-own-behaviour condition under release-contract.md section 3 clause 2, so it is satisfied by owner-machine real processes and is not D1's; condition 3 (roll back without losing shared state) is preview-local live, V2-035, and is blocked on escalation E2; condition 4 (do not delete old binaries or docs while the rollback window is open) is local closure, V2-034.
decisions.rationale: The brief asks which of the six need a real deploy and whether the roadmap agrees. Measured against release-contract.md section 3, only four things require preview-gcp (IAP boundary, scale-to-zero, real Firestore permissions and contention, the deploy path) and none of them is named by an M8 completion condition, so M8 closes at preview-local. Saying so explicitly is what stops V2-035 from being blocked on the GCP work the owner has deliberately deferred, and stops V2-034 from claiming a live result.

decisions.decision: Scope boundary between V2-034 and V2-035. V2-034 owns, and V2-035 must not add: everything in internal/update and cmd/bootstrap named above (accepted schema set, manifest v2 fields, trust anchor resolution and refusals, bootstrap run, per-launch re-verification, confinement probe at launch, monotonic recorded Switch, installed.json, GC predicate and executor, stage machinery and the bounded resumable migrator over an injected port, import guards) plus the runbook. V2-034 must not deploy anything, must not start a real Provider CLI, must not touch GCP or a credential, and must not report any of roadmap M8's conditions 1 to 3 as met; its honest claim is that the local closure refuses the wrong bundle, launches only a re-verified binary, keeps a rollback target and its documents while the window is open, and cannot delete or contract past a still-routable version. V2-035 owns the live half and adds no update semantics: if it finds it needs a new refusal or a new manifest field, it stops and escalates rather than editing internal/update, because a semantics change discovered during a live exercise invalidates the local evidence it was supposed to build on. V2-035 evidence must record environment class preview-local, machine identifiers for both roots or machines, the emulator name and version, kernel version, Provider CLI versions where one is used, and a skip count of zero.
decisions.rationale: The two tasks share one component name (update) but not one environment grade, and G3 distinguishes them by component naming (update versus update-live-self-deploy). A boundary written claim by claim is what prevents V2-034's local evidence from being read as satisfying an M8 completion condition that requires real processes.

decisions.decision: What internal/update is missing today, measured, as the checklist V2-034 must close: (1) no launcher and no exec path at all (verbs are install|switch|--version; nothing in the tree reads root/stable); (2) the trust anchor comes from argv --public-key with no fixed path, no ownership or mode check, no key set and no key id; (3) no re-verification of on-disk bytes before exec, only at install; (4) Switch is an unguarded symlink flip to any installed version, with no record, no monotonicity and no requirement that the forward direction name a gate-passed digest; (5) no GC and no retention state whatsoever, so versions/ grows without bound and there is no rolled_back_at, no window state and no installed-version record; (6) the manifest is closed and single-module (exact schema equality plus DisallowUnknownFields, no accepted set) and carries no bundle_digest, candidate_id, contract_release, runner_api range, key_id or algorithm, so nothing joins a running binary to the gated source tree; (7) no schema migration machinery anywhere in the tree and no owner for the canonical schema counter, while internal/store/firestore compares record_schema with != in both readers, making envelope coexistence impossible; (8) no version reporting: no domain Runner aggregate and no version field on any Runner-facing API request, so a mixed-version period is invisible to canonical state; (9) cmd/bootstrap has no test files at all although make component-runner runs ./cmd/bootstrap, and internal/update has exactly two tests with no fail-closed negative cases beyond tamper and schema interval; (10) the launcher does not consult runner.NamespaceConfinement.Probe, so a child could be started outside the V2-046 confinement; (11) no audit record of install or switch, so 'which version ran when' is unanswerable after an incident.
decisions.rationale: The brief asks for the gap list to be measured rather than assumed, and the list is also the acceptance skeleton for V2-034: each item names a file and a symbol, so a reviewer can check closure without re-reading the design. Items 7 and 8 are the two that cannot be closed inside an update-gated task and therefore appear as escalations E1 and E2 rather than as work.

decisions.decision: Escalations. E1: canonical Runner version reporting does not exist (no domain Runner aggregate, no version field on any Runner-facing request), so the cross-machine interval intersection of d9 cannot be enforced by the Control Plane; owner is the domain/api decision maker, not V2-034. E2: internal/store/firestore's readers accept exactly one record_schema, so envelope-level coexist is impossible; the widening belongs to the store-firestore component and must be assigned before V2-035, which needs it for M8 condition 3. E3: whether Cloud KMS offers an Ed25519 asymmetric-sign algorithm in the target project is a D1-time fact, not a now-fact; the design must therefore allow a second algorithm in the anchor set rather than assume one. E4: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 5 lists only the update component for M8, but the launcher lives in cmd/bootstrap, which is a runner component root, so V2-034's work will move the runner component's evidence key; V2-034 should emit two records (update and runner) as V2-058 did, and the DAG row should say so. None of E1 to E4 may be resolved by editing ci/components.json, the Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.* in this task or in V2-034; those belong to V2-045.
decisions.rationale: An escalation with a named owner and a named blocking relation is actionable; one written as a risk is not. E4 in particular is cheap to fix now and expensive to discover during the M8 gate, when a missing runner-component record would make the gate's freshness check fail for reasons unrelated to the work.

decisions.decision: V2-033 itself is design-only and produces no code. Its deliverable is docs/operations/self-update.md rewritten to carry d2 through d17, plus one evidence record. It may not edit internal/**, cmd/**, contracts/**, ci/**, the Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.*, docs/architecture/** (held open by other agents, and docs/architecture/decisions/index.md would need a Sol-level decision to gain a row), docs/preview/** or docs/stable/**. docs/operations is deliberately the home: it is not one of V2-021's seven bundle roles (the documentation role is docs/preview/**.md and docs/stable/**.md only), so recording measured digests and file paths there cannot create the self-referential digest fixpoint dp-v2-021 d14 prohibits. No key material, no key path containing a secret value, no token and no credential appears in the document. Determinism is an acceptance property inherited by V2-034: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock dependence, no background timer, no goroutine in tests, bounded deadline polling only, injected clock, one top-level function per journey, t.TempDir fixtures.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 5 assigns M8設計 the update component with '設計docのみ', so the packet must not smuggle implementation into the design task; and the fixpoint prohibition is the reason the runbook rather than a Preview document is the right container for measured facts.

verification: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/update ./cmd/bootstrap (timeout 600s): measured baseline for d1; exactly two top-level tests pass and cmd/bootstrap reports '[no test files]'. Re-run unchanged by V2-033.
devbox run --pure -- make component-update (timeout 300s): the update component check stays green with no code change, which is the check the design-only evidence record is entitled to claim.
devbox run --pure -- make component-docs (timeout 300s): no TODO(ci) marker is introduced into the rewritten runbook.
devbox run --pure -- make docs (timeout 300s): the deleted-numbered-document link guard still passes over docs/operations/self-update.md.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts (timeout 600s): TestTaskPacketsValidate accepts both V2-033 packets and TestActiveEvidenceIndex accepts the registered evidence record.
